decisions.reason: The source changes how the second V is constructed. Its general goal of a cohesive alphabet does not modify the established E and L geometry requirements.
The client reaffirms the original approved Hero V as the fixed reference but does not change its geometry or other current attributes.
The optical-matching instruction applies to the second V's right arm and does not alter the requirement that the É accent literally reuse the Hero V terminal geometry.
The source does not discuss or change the exact peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
The source changes the second V's construction method while retaining its supporting role and extended-right-arm signature. The existing hierarchy constraints remain valid unchanged.
The source changes second-V drawing methodology and makes no decision about kerning, pair spacing, or the selected spacing variation.
The client retains the extended right arm as the signature detail and does not change the established terminal intent or its cross-glyph signature role.
Replacing mathematical scaling with optical drawing for the second V does not revoke or modify the rule aligning E and L cap height to its left arm.
The source concerns second-V geometry and does not resume or modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
The source provides design feedback but does not change the obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
The source changes second-V construction without changing the established common-baseline alignment.
The source contains no decision about proof attachment formats or Mac compatibility.
